Folks — copying the redline strategy I discussed with Sarah. High level thoughts:

1) Deletion from live systems: agree to logical deletion within 48 hours of request and physical removal from active databases within 30 days where feasible. That gets Acme the operational assurance they want.

2) Backups/DR: we cannot guarantee immediate purging of backup media (immutable snapshots, tape, object snapshots). Propose a compromise: exclude backups from the immediate deletion obligation but limit retention on backup media to a fixed, time-bound window (we're proposing 13 months / 395 days max) and require restoration/destruction workflows within that time. We should explicitly add a statement that backups are only used for DR and restoration purposes and will not be used for any other processing.

3) EEA transfers: we will reference SCCs + our standard supplementary safeguards. If Acme wants a DPA addendum referencing Schrems assessment, NEHA (Neha) can confirm.

Action items:
- Neha: please craft the exact DPA wording for the backup carveout (concise, contract-ready).
- Marissa: once legal signs off, I'll push the DocuSign envelope to Acme's procurement.

I'll attach our suggested redline.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

> 
> Thanks for the call this morning. Our cyber and procurement teams ran the DPA and have a couple of requested clarifications around deletion and backups before legal can sign...

Sarah — thanks for the clear summary. Laura and I discussed and legal has prepared a short carveout paragraph that we think addresses Acme's operational needs while preserving Redwood's ability to meet DR obligations. Summary (contract language to follow in attached PDF):

- Live deletion: Redwood will implement Customer-initiated logical deletion within 48 hours and will make commercially reasonable efforts to purge Customer Data from active production systems within 30 days, subject to technical constraints.
- Backups/DR carveout: Backup media and DR images are excluded from the immediate deletion requirement solely to allow for disaster recovery and integrity verification. Such backup copies will be retained only for a limited period not to exceed 13 months (395 days) from the date the backup copy was created, after which Redwood will destroy or render the backup copy unrecoverable. The parties agree that backups will not be used for any other processing purpose.
- EEA transfers: Redwood will rely on SCCs and maintain documented transfer risk assessments; Redwood can provide the assessment summary under NDA if needed.

I have attached the DPA with the proposed redline (Redwood_DPA_Acme_v3_for_esign.pdf). If that looks good to you, I'll start the DocuSign envelope. For speed, we're ready to use DocuSign — link below will go live when I create the envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/XYZ-ACME-4582
